react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelmingly dominant biological signal in this dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit at rank 1 with FDR 7.8e-13, powered by 5 of the 8 input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid); fold-enrichment exceeds 833, confirming exceptional pathway specificity. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00380 as its top pathway (p = 5.49e-06) with the identical 4-molecule hit set, providing a fully orthogonal community-standard verification. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis on the empirical human_mfn network independently returns 'Tryptophan metabolism' (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) as its top hit (p = 0.00042) with overlap of 11/12 measured features, confirming network-level activity even without prior annotation. These three independent paradigms (ORA × 2, m/z-direct × 1) together constitute a robust cross-paradigm consensus. Five driver metabolites map to distinct branches of tryptophan catabolism: L-tryptophan (C00078) as the canonical substrate; serotonin (C00780) as the biogenic-amine-branch product; melatonin (C01598) as the N-acetylation product downstream of serotonin; 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) as the key intermediate of the IDO/kynurenine branch; and quinolinic acid (C03722) as the downstream NAD+-precursor from that branch. The treatment group therefore shows coordinated elevation across both the serotonin/melatonin and kynurenine/quinolinate arms of tryptophan catabolism, suggesting broad activation of tryptophan-degradation flux. Two metabolites (O-phosphoethanolamine, 3-methyladenine) did not map to tryptophan metabolism, consistent with their known roles in glycerophospholipid/ethanolamine and purine pathways, respectively.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR 7.8e-13, powered by five metabolites: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as its top pathway with p-value 5.49e-06, sharing the same four-molecule hit set of L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 1 with p-value 0.00025 and overlap of 11 of 12 input features, confirming network-level activity without requiring prior annotation. The four-driver set spans both canonical branches of tryptophan catabolism: the biogenic-amine arm (serotonin and melatonin via TPH1/TTPH2 and ASMT) and the IDO/kynurenine arm (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid via IDO1 and KYNU). The convergent signal across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms supports broad activation of tryptophan-degradation flux in the treatment group, with no other pathway reaching significance in more than one method.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' at FDR 7.80e-13, driven by five metabolites from the input set. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns the same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) at p=5.49e-06 with four overlapping metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis on the human_mfn network confirms the same pathway (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) at p=8.40e-05 with an overlap of 11 of 12 input features, demonstrating network-level activity independent of prior annotation. The convergent five-metabolite driver set includes L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. RaMP ORA additionally identifies two structurally distinct sub-branches of tryptophan degradation: the serotonergic arm mapped to 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR=9.11e-09) and the kynurenine arm mapped to 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (WP:WP4210, FDR=2.95e-11). Both sub-pathways carry independent enrichment signal and together implicate broad dysregulation of tryptophan catabolic flux rather than a single branch.
